orders.text:
SL. 
No Date
Office Notes, reports, 
orders or proceedings 
or directions and 
Registrar’s order with 
Signatures
COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
WPMS No.14 of 2026
Hon’blePankaj Purohit,J.
(through V.C.)
Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for 
petitioner-plaintiff.
2. Mr. K.S. Mehta, learned Additional 
C.S.C. with Mr. Sudhir K. Nailwal, learned 
Standing Counsel and Mr. Bhupendra S. 
Koranga, learned Brief Holder for the State 
of Uttarakhand/respondent No.1.
3. Ms. Anjali Bhargava, learned counsel
for respondent No.2-Gram Sabha.
4. By means of the present writ petition, 
petitioner has challenged the order dated 
25.08.2023 passed by learned Board of 
Revenue, Circuit Bench, Nainital, in Second 
Appeal No.18 of 2015-16 State of 
Uttarakhand and Another Vs. Mahendra 
Singh and Others, whereby, the second 
appeal filed by respondent Nos.1 and 2 
was allowed.
5. It is contended by learned counsel for 
petitioner-plaintiff that the Revenue Suit 
No.22/40 of 2003-04 Mahendra Singh Vs. 
Avtar Singh and Ors., was filed by 
petitioner for declaration of his right as 
Bhumidhar over the land in-question. The 
said Suit was decreed. Petitioner-plaintiff 
pleaded adverse possession against private 
respondent; the first appeal was filed by 
respondent No.1-State and respondent 
No.2-Gram Sabha, therefore, learned First 
Appellate Court was within its right to  dismiss the same. But, surprisingly the 
Second Appeal preferred by respondent 
No.1-State and respondent No.2-Gram 
Sabha, was allowed only on the ground 
that notice under Section 80 of CPC was 
not served upon the respondent No.1-
State Government before filing of suit.
6. Learned counsel for petitioner-plaintiff 
submits that petitioner-plaintiff has been in 
possession of aforesaid land in-question 
since 1366 Fasali and he has filed the Suit 
on the basis of adverse possession.
7. Issue notice to respondent No.3, 
returnable within six weeks.
8. Steps to be taken within 03 days.
9. Put up on 20.03.2026.
10. Meanwhile, respondents may file 
counter affidavit(s).
11. Till the next date of listing, petitioner￾plaintiff shall not be dispossessed from the 
land in-question.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
07.01.2026
PN
